summary: Part 2 of Parkevtate Vosianc's Nike deep dive examines why sales are falling, and he gives no buy, hold or sell verdict in this part — the final verdict is reserved for the members-only Part 5. Sales fell 4% in the most recent quarter and management guides to a negative high-single-digit decline for fiscal 2027, a sharp reversal from the high-single-digit growth Nike compounded through roughly 2010 to 2019. Two headwinds dominate. The Jordan brand, 13% of the business, fell by the mid-teens, partly self-inflicted as Nike restricts supply of popular shoes to create scarcity, a strategy he questions. Greater China fell 26% year over year; Nike is ending discount-heavy distribution partners and cleaning up its digital ecosystem, but management itself expects that cleanup to take multiple seasons, with intense local competition and tariff headwinds in the background. He says he is losing confidence that Nike can turn the business around, noting the turnaround keeps taking longer with no clear inflection, despite the brand, distribution and athlete relationships he once thought would power a recovery. In a digression he mentions he announced in a video that morning that he added to his Netflix position, but makes no Netflix call here.
